description: Explains how pressure differences, rotation, and heating shape winds and global circulation, from geostrophic balance through monsoons, jet streams, and storms.

related_resources.reason: Coriolis, Hadley/Ferrel/polar circulation cells and their simplified structure, shifting rain and pressure belts.
Derivation and interpretation of vertical geostrophic shear and horizontal layer-mean temperature gradients.
ITCZ, Hadley cell, subtropical descent, midlatitude westerlies and monsoon-like seasonal geographic influences.
Section 2.1.2: Ferrel cells as eddy-driven, thermally indirect mean circulations; midlatitude storms carry poleward energy.
Temperature gradients, upper-air jets, seasonal shifts, storms and variable wave structure.
Large-scale Rossby waves and their relationship to jet-stream meanders and the development of weather systems.
Global humidity response, precipitation energy constraints, water cycle variability and global versus regional patterns.
Balloon-borne radiosonde measurements of pressure, temperature, humidity, wind and vertical atmospheric structure.

historical_claims.anchor: a horizontal pressure difference tends to accelerate air from higher pressure toward lower pressure
historical_claims.source_locator: Pressure differences drive flow; educational global circulation discussion.

historical_claims.anchor: It points to the right of the motion in the Northern Hemisphere
Meteorologists call the resulting approximate flow geostrophic
historical_claims.source_locator: Geostrophic balance used as a prerequisite in atmospheric thermal-wind derivation.

historical_claims.anchor: This overturning is called the Hadley circulation
The Sahara is not simply a laboratory sample of latitude thirty north
historical_claims.source_locator: Latitude-associated subsidence is schematic; regional land/ocean/topography also matter.

historical_claims.anchor: the Ferrel cell is closely tied to the net effects of midlatitude eddies
historical_claims.source_locator: Review section 2.1.2 on indirect, eddy-driven Ferrel circulation.
Vertical geostrophic wind shear linked to horizontal temperature gradient.

historical_claims.anchor: The jet streams provide another view of the same dynamics
historical_claims.source_locator: Upper-air strong wind corridors near temperature contrasts.
Large-scale meandering jets and wave pattern; general dynamical context.

historical_claims.anchor: When the vapor later condenses into cloud droplets, latent heat is released
historical_claims.source_locator: Water cycle and atmospheric latent heating.

historical_claims.anchor: The South Asian monsoon links the heated land mass and surrounding oceans
historical_claims.source_locator: Regional moisture and seasonal atmospheric circulation.

historical_claims.anchor: Weather balloons carry sensors through the troposphere
historical_claims.source_locator: Upper-air observation and vertical wind profiling; general observational context.

background: Pressure and temperature are introduced from first principles; no prior dynamical meteorology required.
readiness_checks: Why does rotation change the direction of wind without supplying its energy?
Why are midlatitude weather systems essential to the Ferrel cell?
How does latent-heat release change the development of rising air?
Why does a jet stream map not uniquely determine the cause of a flood?
